title: Tinnie's Water Hole / Napeague Beach
summary: Tooker recorded Tinnie's as a water hole on Napeague Beach near the Amagansett Hills. The historic water hole has not been matched to a named modern pond, so this marker represents the broader Napeague beach and dune landscape.
address_label: Napeague State Park, East Hampton, NY (broad representative point)
map_geometry_source: Representative Napeague State Park point based on Tooker's Napeague Beach and Amagansett Hills description and official New York State park mapping; exact water hole unknown.
why_this_matters: The name records a small water feature within the Napeague coastal landscape and a story about a woman whose identity was not preserved in the printed account. A broad marker keeps the record searchable without inventing an exact pond or treating an unverified story as established fact.
introduction_title: A Water Hole on Napeague Beach
introduction_content: The surviving description places Tinnie's on Napeague Beach near the Amagansett Hills. Modern state maps confirm the Napeague State Park landscape between Amagansett and Hither Hills, but they do not preserve Tinnie's as a mapped water feature.
history_content: Tooker repeated a story that the place was named for a Native woman who drowned there. He did not identify her or provide an earlier source for the story, so the listing preserves it only as an unverified historical account and does not repeat his outdated terminology for her.
translation_content: Tinnie's appears as a personal place name rather than a translated Indigenous landscape term. No secure alternate spelling or modern water-body identification has been found.
preservation_content: This draft retains the references while keeping an uncertain and sensitive story off the public map until reviewed.
whereintheworld_content: The marker is placed broadly in Napeague State Park near the Atlantic beach and Amagansett side of the Napeague stretch. It is an orientation point for the historic landscape, not the recovered location of the former water hole.
